option_c_en: Direct administration by the Union Home Ministry

(A) Creation of a Special Administrative Tribunal for Civil Services (B) Exclusive reservation of 80% seats in all central universities (C) Direct administration by the Union Home Ministry (D) Complete exemption from NJAC guidelines
normalized_question_text: Under Article 371-D of the Constitution of India, which of the following provisions was specifically created for the State of Andhra Pradesh?

reason_summary: Evaluates the candidate's understanding of constitutional safeguards unique to the region, which is critical for aspiring police personnel responsible for administrative law enforcement.

question_en: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the Election Commission?

question_en:
Consider the following statements regarding the Kakatiya dynasty architectural heritage in Telangana:
1. The Ramappa Temple at Palampet was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2021 as the 39th site of India.
2. The temple is constructed using lightweight porous bricks known as "floating bricks" and a sandbox foundation technique.
3. The temple was commissioned by King Ganapati Deva and built under the supervision of his general Recharla Rudra in 1213 CE.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
answer_source_citation: TGPSC Final Key Revised: Master Series A Q2 changed from provisional A to FINAL C after examining 1213 CE inscription records.
provisional_conflict_history: Provisional Answer Key initially indicated Option A (claiming statement 3 was disputed). Final Expert Committee verified the 1213 CE Palampet inscription attributing construction to Recharla Rudra under Ganapati Deva, revising Final Key to C (1, 2 and 3).
raw_question_text: Consider the following statements regarding the Kakatiya dynasty architectural heritage in Telangana: 1. The Ramappa Temple at Palampet was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2021 as the 39th site of India. 2. The temple is constructed using lightweight porous bricks known as "floating bricks" and a sandbox foundation technique. 3. The temple was commissioned by King Ganapati Deva and built under the supervision of his general Recharla Rudra in 1213 CE. Which of the statements given above are correct? (A) 1 and 2 only (B) 2 and 3 only (C) 1, 2 and 3 (D) 1 and 3 only
normalized_question_text: Consider the statements regarding Ramappa Temple: 1. UNESCO list 2021 as 39th site. 2. Floating bricks & sandbox foundation. 3. Commissioned by Ganapati Deva / General Recharla Rudra in 1213 CE.

difficulty_factors.knowledge_obscurity: Requires precise knowledge of UNESCO year, engineering design, and 1213 CE inscription records
difficulty_factors.statement_complexity: Three factual statements requiring tripartite confirmation

source_domain: Archaeological Survey of India & UNESCO World Heritage Dossier

distractor_details.option_a_trap: Traps students who doubted the exact epigraph date (1213 CE) or commander name (Recharla Rudra)
distractor_details.option_b_trap: Omits statement 1 (UNESCO 2021) which is widely known, tempting students who only memorized textbook history
distractor_details.option_d_trap: Omits the famous sandbox foundation / floating bricks engineering novelty

reason_summary: Ramappa Temple was inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage Site in July 2021, turning this core medieval Kakatiya architecture chapter into a high-priority question theme for state examinations.

question_en:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the sentence:
"He did not know nothing about the sudden change in the management's policy."
answer_source_citation: SSC CGL Tier-I Official Master Key, Section 4 Q17: Option B (did not know anything)
raw_question_text: did not know nothing -> (A) knew nothing (B) did not know anything (C) was not knowing (D) know nothing
normalized_question_text: Avoid double negatives in formal English: "did not know anything" or "knew nothing". Idiomatic past negative is "did not know anything".

difficulty_factors.knowledge_obscurity: Double negative rule in standard English
difficulty_factors.statement_complexity: Eliminating redundancy while preserving past tense auxiliary

distractor_details.option_a_trap: Grammatically possible but shifts cadence; standard replacement is B
distractor_details.option_b_trap: Correct: Replaces erroneous double negative "did not know nothing" with "did not know anything"
distractor_details.option_c_trap: Stative verb "know" cannot be used in continuous tense ("was knowing")
distractor_details.option_d_trap: Present tense without auxiliary creates tense clash

reason_summary: Double negative avoidance and stative verb non-continuous rules are standard SSC English items.

adjacent_concepts.concept: Hardly/Scarcely with "when" (Inversion rule)
adjacent_concepts.relationship_to_pyq: Semi-negative adverb usage rule

core_concept: Elimination of double negatives in English syntax
core_answerable_fact: In standard English, auxiliary negative "did not" requires non-negative indefinite pronoun "anything"
relationships: "did not know anything" eliminates double negative

question_en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom:
"Burn the candle at both ends"
option_a_en: To waste money on luxury items and live lavishly
option_b_en: To work extremely hard from early morning until late night
option_c_en: To create unnecessary trouble and quarrels for others
option_d_en: To illuminate a dark room using multiple light sources
answer_source_citation: SSC CGL Tier-I Official Master Key, Section 4 Q18: Option B (To work extremely hard...)
raw_question_text: Burn candle at both ends: (A) waste money (B) work hard early morning to late night (C) create trouble (D) illuminate
normalized_question_text: Idiom "burn candle at both ends" means to exhaust oneself by doing too much work and sleeping little.
microtopic: Metaphorical Meaning of Candle Burning at Both Ends

distractor_details.option_a_trap: Confuses with "burn a hole in one's pocket"
distractor_details.option_b_trap: Correct: Means to overwork oneself by getting up early and staying up late
distractor_details.option_c_trap: Confuses with "stir up a hornet's nest"

reason_summary: Idioms concerning effort, time, and human behavior appear 2-3 times per SSC CGL shift.

adjacent_concepts.concept: Burn the midnight oil (To study or work late into the night)
adjacent_concepts.relationship_to_pyq: Synonymous effort/work idiom

core_concept: Metaphorical meaning of "burn the candle at both ends"
core_answerable_fact: "Burn the candle at both ends" means to work relentlessly from dawn to late at night with little rest
entities: Burn the candle at both ends
relationships: Idiom signifies working extremely hard without adequate rest
correct_answer_concept: To work extremely hard from early morning until late night

question_en:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words:
"A person who donates time and money to help make the world a better place and promotes the welfare of others"
answer_source_citation: SSC CGL Tier-I Official Master Key, Section 4 Q19: Option A (Philanthropist)
raw_question_text: One who donates money to help others: (A) Philanthropist (B) Misanthrope (C) Polyglot (D) Recluse
normalized_question_text: Philanthropist: a person who seeks to promote the welfare of others, especially by generous donation of money to good causes.

difficulty_factors.distractor_similarity: Common Greek root words describing human types

distractor_details.option_a_trap: Correct: From Phil (love) + anthropos (mankind)
distractor_details.option_b_trap: Opposite meaning: Misanthrope is one who hates or distrusts humankind
distractor_details.option_c_trap: Polyglot is a person who knows or uses several languages
distractor_details.option_d_trap: Recluse is a person who lives a solitary life and tends to avoid other people

reason_summary: One Word Substitutions with Greek/Latin root words (phil-, mis-, anthrop-) are perennial SSC favorites.

adjacent_concepts.concept: Altruist (Unselfish concern for welfare of others) and Benefactor
adjacent_concepts.relationship_to_pyq: Synonymous human attribute substitutes

core_concept: Etymology of Philanthropist (love of humanity)
core_answerable_fact: A Philanthropist is one who promotes human welfare through benevolent giving and service
relationships: Philanthropist denotes a promoter of human welfare
